n: Nicodemus is a Pharisee and a member of the ruling council — a respected, learned leader. He appears three times in John, and his faith seems to grow each time.

f.g: A Greek name meaning “victor over the people.”
A member of the Sanhedrin, the Jewish high council.

n: He comes at night — perhaps to avoid being seen, or simply for an uninterrupted conversation. He acknowledges that Jesus’ miracles show God is with Him.

f.g: In John, night often hints at spiritual darkness someone is coming out of.
A sincere but incomplete view of Jesus.

n: Jesus goes straight to the heart: unless a person is born again, they cannot see God’s kingdom. A fresh spiritual start is required, not just admiration.

f.g: Greek anōthen means both “again” and “from above.”

n: Nicodemus takes it literally: how can a grown man re-enter his mother’s womb? His question shows how foreign the idea of spiritual rebirth is to him.

f.g: Perhaps Nicodemus is also asking how an older man can truly change.

n: Jesus explains: one must be born of water and of the Spirit — baptism by immersion and the gift of the Holy Ghost — to enter God’s kingdom. Both ordinances are essential.

f.w: born of water and of the Spirit

n: Physical birth produces physical life; spiritual birth produces spiritual life. Each kind of birth brings its own kind of life.
Don’t be surprised, Jesus says, that I told you all must be born again. The “ye” is plural — this applies to everyone.

f.g: Don’t be amazed.

n: The wind blows wherever it wants; you hear it but can’t see where it comes from or goes. The Spirit works the same way — invisible, yet its effects are real.

f.g: In Greek (pneuma) and Hebrew (ruach), the same word means both “wind” and “spirit.”
Wishes, chooses.

n: Nicodemus is still puzzled: how can these things happen?
Jesus gently challenges him: you’re a respected teacher of Israel and don’t understand this? The prophets spoke of a new heart and spirit.

f.g: “The teacher of Israel” — a prominent religious instructor.

n: We speak about what we know and testify of what we have seen, Jesus says, yet you don’t accept our testimony.

f.w: We speak that we do know

n: If you don’t believe when I describe earthly things, like birth and wind, how will you believe heavenly realities?

f.g: Deeper truths about God and eternity.

n: No one has gone up to heaven except the one who came down from it — the Son of Man. Jesus speaks with firsthand knowledge of heaven.

f.w: he that came down from heaven

f.g: Missing in some early manuscripts.

n: When Israel was dying from snakebites, Moses raised a bronze serpent on a pole, and all who looked lived. So the Son of Man must be lifted up on the cross.

f.w: as Moses lifted up the serpent

n: ...so that everyone who believes in Him will have eternal life. As with the serpent, the cure is to look in faith.

f.g: In John, both a quality of life now and life with God forever.

n: Perhaps the most beloved verse in the Bible: God loved the world so much that He gave His Only Begotten Son, so that whoever believes in Him will not perish but have everlasting life.
God didn’t send His Son to condemn the world but to save it. Christ’s mission is rescue.

f.w: not his Son into the world to condemn the world

n: Whoever believes in Him escapes condemnation. Whoever refuses to believe stands condemned already — not because God rejects them, but because they reject the remedy.
Here is the judgment: the Light came into the world, but people preferred darkness because their actions were evil.

f.w: men loved darkness rather than light

n: Those who do evil hate the light and avoid it, so their actions won’t be exposed.

f.g: Exposed and shown to be wrong.

n: But those who live by the truth come to the light, gladly letting it show that their deeds were done through God.

f.g: Done in God’s strength and in harmony with Him.

f.w: he that doeth truth cometh to the light

n: Jesus and His disciples go out into the Judean countryside, where He spends time with them and baptizes. John 4:2 clarifies that His disciples performed the baptisms under His direction.

f.g: Stayed.

n: John the Baptist is still baptizing at Aenon near Salim, because there is plenty of water there — a detail suggesting baptism by immersion.

f.g: “Springs” — probably in the Jordan Valley.

f.w: because there was much water there

n: This happened before John was imprisoned by Herod Antipas.
A debate arises between some of John’s disciples and a Jewish man about ritual purification — likely about the meaning of baptism.

f.g: Many manuscripts read “a Jew.”
Ceremonial cleansing rituals.

n: John’s disciples come to him concerned: the man you testified about is baptizing, and everyone is going to Him! They feel their teacher is being overshadowed.

f.g: An exaggeration showing their worry.

n: John answers humbly: a person can receive only what heaven gives him. Each has his own God-given role.

f.w: except it be given him from heaven

n: You yourselves heard me say I am not the Messiah but the one sent ahead of Him.
John uses a wedding image: the bride belongs to the groom. The best man doesn’t envy him — he rejoices to hear the groom’s voice. John’s joy is complete in seeing Christ succeed.

f.g: In scripture, God is pictured as the bridegroom of His people.
Like the best man, who arranged the wedding.

n: John’s famous words: He must increase, but I must decrease. A model of humility for every servant of Christ.
The one from above is over all. Earthly people speak from an earthly viewpoint; the one from heaven is supreme. Some scholars think verses 31–36 are the Gospel writer’s reflections.
He testifies of what He has personally seen and heard in heaven, yet few accept His testimony.

f.g: A generalization — relatively few, not literally none (see v. 33).

n: Whoever accepts His testimony puts a seal on it, certifying that God is true. Believing Christ is affirming God’s truthfulness.

f.g: Certified, as with a wax seal on a document.

n: The one God sent speaks God’s words, for God gives Him the Spirit without limit. The JST adds that the Spirit dwells in Him in fulness.

f.g: Without limit. JST John 3:34 adds: “for he dwelleth in him, even the fulness.”

n: The Father loves the Son and has entrusted everything into His hands.

f.w: hath given all things into his hand

n: Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life; whoever refuses to obey the Son will not see life, and God’s judgment remains on them. Belief and obedience go together.

f.g: Greek apeitheō — “disobeys,” refuses to obey.
God’s righteous judgment against sin.
